prediction.likelyOutcome: Barham should recover at least the $163,000 court-appointed appraisal for the physical taking, and has a credible — though genuinely contested — shot at additional compensation for the extinguished Threel Road ingress-egress easement given that summary judgment was denied on that exact theory. Without an expert diminution-in-value appraisal in the record, however, that upside component cannot be responsibly quantified, so the case's provable floor value sits close to the appraised figure while its true upside could be materially larger once (if) that evidence is developed.

Compensability of Extinguished Threel Road Ingress-Egress Easement
Wrong-Forum / Attribution Defense (County Line Action vs. This Case)
Statutory Litigation Expenses / Fee-Shifting on Appraisal Rejection

outcome.description: After a May 2022 jury trial the Marion Circuit Court entered judgment on a $2.4 million verdict for Barham and denied Carmel's motions to correct error, for new trial, and for remittitur. The Court of Appeals reversed on October 30, 2023, holding Barham had no compensable easement interest in Threel Road (already extinguished in the County Line condemnation) and that the access change was non-compensable under the ingress-egress and traffic-flow rules, and remanded with instructions to grant Carmel partial summary judgment on that issue.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed and remanded; no final figure yet.
